analysis.investment_thesis: Pajson Agro is a tiny, recently incorporated (2021) cashew processor with an unacceptable 0.60% ROE yet trading at 18.3x P/E — a combination I cannot justify. Cashew processing is a low-margin, commodity-linked, working-capital-heavy business with no moat; I see no reason to own this.
key_strengths: DII holding 7.63% indicates some institutional interest
key_risks: ROE of 0.60% is abysmal — far below my 15%+ threshold
Commodity cashew processing has no pricing power or moat
Incorporated only in 2021 — no track record across cycles
red_flags: P/E 18.3x vs ROE 0.60% is a grossly mispriced combination
Micro-cap (Rs 374 Cr) newly listed SME-type stock with thin disclosure
Earnings quality and margin sustainability unproven
analysis.detailed_analysis: This fails my most basic quality screen. A 0.60% ROE means the business is barely earning anything on shareholder capital — in cashew processing, margins are thin, inventory cycles are long, and forex/commodity swings routinely wipe out profits. Paying 18.3x earnings for a business earning sub-1% on equity is effectively paying a quality multiple for a sub-par asset. Good businesses in my portfolio earn 18-22% ROE consistently; this is two orders of magnitude off.
